title: Loop Termination
definition: Loop termination requires a reachable exit condition and state changes that make progress toward it.
purpose: Prevent unintended non-termination and justify that finite input processing eventually stops.
history: Termination and invariant reasoning are central topics in algorithm correctness and formal program reasoning.
mental_model: Name a non-negative distance to the exit and show that every round makes that distance strictly smaller until the condition becomes false.
analogy: A countdown reaches zero if each round subtracts one; it fails for irregular state spaces or updates that can move away from the exit.
industry_notes: Operational safeguards such as timeouts complement but do not replace correct termination design.
ai_notes: Demand an explicit variant or bounded-input argument for AI-generated loops.
interview_notes: Ask what changes, why it approaches exit, and which inputs violate assumptions.
